newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended down slightly on Tuesday as investors took profits after a two percent rise in the index on Monday, brokers said.
Trading was relatively slow because investors were waiting for more 1997 interim results, which listed companies must report by the end of August, they said.
The B share index fell 0.041 points or 0.05 percent to 77.332 points on volume of 8.567 million shares worth $5.262 million.
"The market is taking a breather after a few days of galloping up," said an analyst at a European securities firm in Shanghai.
B shares fell on Tuesday after failing to break resistance at 78 points, brokers said. The absence of major foreign buying also caused the market's climb to run out of steam, they said.
"After yesterday's gains, the market consolidated today with some profit-taking seen," said a broker at a foreign securities firm.
"Overseas buying was limited and domestic investors are still the major force on the market," he said.
The first Shanghai-listed B share company has already announced interim results for the first half of 1997, and other firms are required to report by the end of August.
Some investors also pulled money out of the market in anticipation of a new share issue, brokers said.
Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd said on Monday it had fixed the price of its 100 million B share issue at $0.433 per share, and the stock would be offered from Tuesday to Thursday.
Of 45 B shares, 39 traded with 22 down, 13 up and four flat.
